name: Can a side addition become an attached ADU in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Can a side addition become an attached ADU in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Can a side addition become an attached ADU in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a side addition can sometimes be designed as an attached ADU, but it must meet the rules for that specific use rather than functioning as a normal room addition. The space generally needs appropriate living functions, code-compliant access, and a layout that supports independent occupancy expectations. Depending on the jurisdiction, the project may also need separate utility planning, fire-rated construction details, and clear separation from the main dwelling’s private areas. Some side-yard additions are good candidates because they can create a compact unit without consuming the rear yard. Others are better treated as a family room, bedroom suite, or office because the site does not support the necessary layout. The most common mistake is assuming any addition with a bathroom qualifies. It does not. The design should be checked early for size limits, ingress and egress, parking impacts if any, and local approval requirements before plans are finalized.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a side addition can sometimes be designed as an attached ADU if it meets local rules for separate living space, access, utilities, and size limits. It cannot simply be labeled an ADU; the layout, entrances, and code compliance must support that use.
